security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, write_menvcfg() and write_henvcfg() do not call tlb_flush() when the ADUE bit changes. QEMU's soft TLB retains cached translations created under the old ADUE interpretation, serving them on TLB hit without re-walking the page table. The spec requires software to execute SFENCE.VMA (or HFENCE.VVMA) after changing ADUE, but QEMU has no defensive mechanism to detect or prevent guest software that omits this synchronization — stale A/D side-effects persist until the guest explicitly fences.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: write_menvcfg|write_henvcfg with MENVCFG_ADUE|HENVCFG_ADUE mask but no tlb_flush or tb_flush call after menvcfg/henvcfg update; ADUE bit read in page table walker without corresponding TLB invalidation on CSR write path
security_spec.summary: QEMU defers TLB invalidation entirely to guest software on menvcfg.ADUE/henvcfg.ADUE changes per spec, but stale soft-TLB entries can serve translations with incorrect A/D side-effects until explicit SFENCE.VMA, risking guest data corruption from lost dirty-page tracking
